sanskrit: ekaśṛṅgaḥ purā bhūtvā varāho divyadarśanaḥ imām uddhṛtavān bhūmim ekaśṛṅgas tato hy aham
english: Of old, having become the single-tusked boar of divine aspect, I lifted up this earth; and thus am I called Ekaśṛṅga, the One-Tusked.

sanskrit: tathaivāsaṃ trikakudo vārāhaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ trikakut tena vikhyātaḥ śarīrasya tu māpanāt
english: Likewise was I Trikakud, having taken on the boar's form; through the measure of that body I became renowned as Trikakud, the Three-Peaked.

sanskrit: viriñca iti yaḥ proktaḥ kapilajñānacintakaiḥ sa prajāpatir evāhaṃ cetanāt sarvalokakṛt
english: He who is named Viriñca by those who ponder the wisdom of Kapila — that very Prajāpati am I, the maker of all the worlds out of consciousness.

sanskrit: vidyāsahāyavantaṃ mām ādityasthaṃ sanātanam kapilaṃ prāhur ācāryāḥ sāṃkhyā niścitaniścayāḥ
english: Me, attended by knowledge, eternal, abiding in the sun, the teachers of Sāṃkhya, firm in their settled certainties, call Kapila.

sanskrit: hiraṇyagarbho dyutimān eṣa yaś chandasi stutaḥ yogaiḥ saṃpūjyate nityaṃ sa evāhaṃ vibhuḥ smṛtaḥ
english: That radiant Hiraṇyagarbha who is praised in the sacred metres and is ever worshipped by the masters of yoga — that very one am I, remembered as the all-pervading Lord.

sanskrit: ekaviṃśatiśākhaṃ ca ṛgvedaṃ māṃ pracakṣate sahasraśākhaṃ yat sāma ye vai vedavido janāḥ gāyanty āraṇyake viprā madbhaktās te 'pi durlabhāḥ
english: Those who know the Vedas declare me to be the Ṛgveda of twenty-one branches, and the Sāman of a thousand branches; and the brāhmaṇas devoted to me who chant the Āraṇyaka — even these are hard to find.

sanskrit: ṣaṭpañcāśatam aṣṭau ca saptatriṃśatam ity uta yasmiñ śākhā yajurvede so 'ham ādhvaryave smṛtaḥ
english: That Yajurveda in which the branches number fifty-six, and eight, and thirty-seven — that am I, remembered in the office of the Adhvaryu priest.

sanskrit: pañcakalpam atharvāṇaṃ kṛtyābhiḥ paribṛṃhitam kalpayanti hi māṃ viprā atharvāṇavidas tathā
english: The brāhmaṇas learned in the Atharvan ordain me likewise as the Atharvaveda of five ritual procedures, swollen full with its rites of sorcery.

sanskrit: śākhābhedāś ca ye ke cid yāś ca śākhāsu gītayaḥ svaravarṇasamuccārāḥ sarvāṃs tān viddhi matkṛtān
english: Whatever divisions of the branches there are, and whatever chants are sung within those branches, and the utterance of their tones and syllables — know all these to be made by me.

sanskrit: yat tad dhayaśiraḥ pārtha samudeti varapradam so 'ham evottare bhāge kramākṣaravibhāgavit
english: That Horse-Headed form, O Pārtha, which rises up bestowing boons — that am I myself in the northern quarter, knower of the divisions of the syllable-sequence.

sanskrit: rāmādeśitamārgeṇa matprasādān mahātmanā pāñcālena kramaḥ prāptas tasmād bhūtāt sanātanāt bābhravyagotraḥ sa babhau prathamaḥ kramapāragaḥ
english: By the path taught by Rāma, through my grace, the great-souled Pāñcāla obtained the krama-recitation from that eternal Being; and he of the Bābhravya lineage shone forth as the first who reached the far shore of the krama.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇād varaṃ labdhvā prāpya yogam anuttamam kramaṃ praṇīya śikṣāṃ ca praṇayitvā sa gālavaḥ
english: Having received a boon from Nārāyaṇa and attained the supreme yoga, that Gālava set forth the krama-recitation and composed the science of phonetics.

sanskrit: kaṇḍarīko 'tha rājā ca brahmadattaḥ pratāpavān jātīmaraṇajaṃ duḥkhaṃ smṛtvā smṛtvā punaḥ punaḥ saptajātiṣu mukhyatvād yogānāṃ saṃpadaṃ gataḥ
english: And Kaṇḍarīka, and the mighty King Brahmadatta, recalling again and again the suffering born of birth and death, attained the fullness of the yogas through their eminence across seven births.

sanskrit: purāham ātmajaḥ pārtha prathitaḥ kāraṇāntare dharmasya kuruśārdūla tato 'haṃ dharmajaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Of old, O Pārtha, for a certain cause I was made known as the son of Dharma, O tiger of the Kurus; and thus am I remembered as Dharmaja, Dharma-born.

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇau pūrvaṃ tapas tepatur avyayam dharmayānaṃ samārūḍhau parvate gandhamādane
english: In ancient days Nara and Nārāyaṇa, mounted upon the vehicle of dharma, performed imperishable austerity upon Mount Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: tatkālasamayaṃ caiva dakṣayajño babhūva ha na caivākalpayad bhāgaṃ dakṣo rudrasya bhārata
english: At that very season came to pass the sacrifice of Dakṣa; and Dakṣa apportioned no share to Rudra, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato dadhīcivacanād dakṣayajñam apāharat sasarja śūlaṃ krodhena prajvalantaṃ muhur muhuḥ
english: Then, at the word of Dadhīci, he carried off Dakṣa's sacrifice; in wrath he hurled his trident, blazing forth again and again.

sanskrit: tac chūlaṃ bhasmasāt kṛtvā dakṣayajñaṃ savistaram āvayoḥ sahasāgacchad badaryāśramam antikāt vegena mahatā pārtha patan nārāyaṇorasi
english: That trident, having reduced Dakṣa's sacrifice in its full extent to ashes, came rushing all at once toward the hermitage of Badarī, near to us both, falling with great force, O Pārtha, upon the breast of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ svatejasāviṣṭāḥ keśā nārāyaṇasya ha babhūvur muñjavarṇās tu tato 'haṃ muñjakeśavān
english: Then the hairs of Nārāyaṇa, suffused with his own fiery splendour, took on the colour of muñja-grass; and thus am I called Muñjakeśa, he of the muñja-coloured hair.

sanskrit: tac ca śūlaṃ vinirdhūtaṃ huṃkāreṇa mahātmanā jagāma śaṃkarakaraṃ nārāyaṇasamāhatam
english: And that trident, flung back by the great-souled one with a sound of 'Huṃ' and struck aside by Nārāyaṇa, returned to the hand of Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: atha rudra upādhāvat tāv ṛṣī tapasānvitau tata enaṃ samuddhūtaṃ kaṇṭhe jagrāha pāṇinā nārāyaṇaḥ sa viśvātmā tenāsya śitikaṇṭhatā
english: Then Rudra rushed upon those two sages endowed with austerity; and Nārāyaṇa, the Soul of all, seized him as he sprang up, by the throat with his hand — and from that came Rudra's dark-throated state.

sanskrit: atha rudravighātārtham iṣīkāṃ jagṛhe naraḥ mantraiś ca saṃyuyojāśu so 'bhavat paraśur mahān
english: Then, to ward off Rudra, Nara took up a blade of reed-grass and swiftly charged it with sacred formulas; and it became a mighty axe.

sanskrit: kṣiptaś ca sahasā rudre khaṇḍanaṃ prāptavāṃs tadā tato 'haṃ khaṇḍaparaśuḥ smṛtaḥ paraśukhaṇḍanāt
english: Cast suddenly at Rudra, it then met with breaking; and thus am I remembered as Khaṇḍaparaśu, he of the Broken Axe, from the shattering of that axe.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca asmin yuddhe tu vārṣṇeya trailokyamathane tadā jayaṃ kaḥ prāptavāṃs tatra śaṃsaitan me janārdana
english: Arjuna said: But in this battle, O Vārṣṇeya, this churning of the three worlds, who then won the victory there? Declare this to me, Janārdana.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca tayoḥ saṃlagnayor yuddhe rudranārāyaṇātmanoḥ udvignāḥ sahasā kṛtsnā lokāḥ sarve 'bhavaṃs tadā
english: The blessed Lord said: When those two, Rudra and Nārāyaṇa in their persons, were locked in combat, all the worlds entire grew suddenly stricken with dread.

sanskrit: nāgṛhṇāt pāvakaḥ śubhraṃ makheṣu suhutaṃ haviḥ vedā na pratibhānti sma ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: The fire would not accept the bright oblation duly offered in the sacrifices; the Vedas no longer shone forth for the sages of disciplined soul.

sanskrit: devān rajas tamaś caiva samāviviśatus tadā vasudhā saṃcakampe 'tha nabhaś ca vipaphāla ha
english: Passion and darkness then entered into the gods alike; the earth trembled, and the firmament split asunder.

sanskrit: niṣprabhāṇi ca tejāṃsi brahmā caivāsanāc cyutaḥ agāc choṣaṃ samudraś ca himavāṃś ca vyaśīryata
english: The luminaries lost their radiance, and Brahmā himself was cast down from his seat; the ocean went dry, and the Himālaya crumbled away.

sanskrit: tasminn evaṃ samutpanne nimitte pāṇḍunandana brahmā vṛto devagaṇair ṛṣibhiś ca mahātmabhiḥ ājagāmāśu taṃ deśaṃ yatra yuddham avartata
english: When such a portent had thus arisen, O son of Pāṇḍu, Brahmā, encircled by the hosts of gods and by the great-souled sages, came swiftly to that place where the battle was being waged.

sanskrit: sāñjalipragraho bhūtvā caturvaktro niruktagaḥ uvāca vacanaṃ rudraṃ lokānām astu vai śivam nyasyāyudhāni viśveśa jagato hitakāmyayā
english: The Four-Faced one, versed in the etymologies, with joined palms held forth, spoke these words to Rudra: 'Let there be welfare for the worlds; lay down your weapons, O Lord of the Universe, for the desire of the good of all that is.'

sanskrit: yad akṣaram athāvyaktam īśaṃ lokasya bhāvanam kūṭasthaṃ kartṛnirdvaṃdvam akarteti ca yaṃ viduḥ
english: 'That which is the Imperishable and the Unmanifest, the Lord, the source of the world, fixed upon its summit, the agent free of all duality, whom they also know as the non-agent —'

sanskrit: vyaktibhāvagatasyāsya ekā mūrtir iyaṃ śivā naro nārāyaṇaś caiva jātau dharmakulodvahau
english: '— of this Being come into manifest form, this is one auspicious embodiment: Nara and Nārāyaṇa, born to uphold the lineage of Dharma.'

sanskrit: tapasā mahatā yuktau devaśreṣṭhau mahāvratau ahaṃ prasādajas tasya kasmiṃś cit kāraṇāntare tvaṃ caiva krodhajas tāta pūrvasarge sanātanaḥ
english: 'Joined with mighty austerity, foremost of gods, mighty in their vows — I was born of his grace upon some occasion, and you yourself, my son, the eternal one, were born of his wrath in the former creation.'

sanskrit: mayā ca sārdhaṃ varadaṃ vibudhaiś ca maharṣibhiḥ prasādayāśu lokānāṃ śāntir bhavatu māciram
english: 'Together with me and with the gods and the great sages, swiftly conciliate the boon-giver, that peace may come to the worlds without delay.'

sanskrit: brahmaṇā tv evam uktas tu rudraḥ krodhāgnim utsṛjan prasādayām āsa tato devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum śaraṇaṃ ca jagāmādyaṃ vareṇyaṃ varadaṃ harim
english: Thus addressed by Brahmā, Rudra let go the fire of his wrath and then conciliated the divine Lord Nārāyaṇa, and took refuge in Hari, the primal, the most excellent, the giver of boons.

sanskrit: tato 'tha varado devo jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ prītimān abhavat tatra rudreṇa saha saṃgataḥ
english: Then the boon-giving god, his anger conquered and his senses mastered, became gladdened there, reconciled together with Rudra.

sanskrit: ṛṣibhir brahmaṇā caiva vibudhaiś ca supūjitaḥ uvāca devam īśānam īśaḥ sa jagato hariḥ
english: Well honoured by the sages and by Brahmā and the gods, that Hari, the Lord of the world, spoke to the god Īśāna:

sanskrit: yas tvāṃ vetti sa māṃ vetti yas tvām anu sa mām anu nāvayor antaraṃ kiṃ cin mā te bhūd buddhir anyathā
english: 'He who knows you knows me; he who follows you follows me. Between us two there is no difference whatever; let your understanding not be otherwise.'

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti śrīvatsaḥ śūlāṅko 'yaṃ bhavatv ayam mama pāṇyaṅkitaś cāpi śrīkaṇṭhas tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi
english: 'From this day forward let this Śrīvatsa mark of mine bear the sign of the trident; and marked by my hand, you shall become Śrīkaṇṭha, the Glorious-Throated.'

sanskrit: evaṃ lakṣaṇam utpādya parasparakṛtaṃ tadā sakhyaṃ caivātulaṃ kṛtvā rudreṇa sahitāv ṛṣī tapas tepatur avyagrau visṛjya tridivaukasaḥ
english: Having thus brought into being these mutually given marks, and having made an unmatched friendship with Rudra, the two sages, untroubled, dismissed the dwellers of heaven and performed their austerities.

sanskrit: eṣa te kathitaḥ pārtha nārāyaṇajayo mṛdhe nāmāni caiva guhyāni niruktāni ca bhārata ṛṣibhiḥ kathitānīha yāni saṃkīrtitāni te
english: Thus has the victory of Nārāyaṇa in battle been told to you, O Pārtha, and the secret names with their etymologies, O Bhārata, which were spoken here by the sages and which have been proclaimed to you.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhai rūpaiś carāmīha vasuṃdharām brahmalokaṃ ca kaunteya golokaṃ ca sanātanam mayā tvaṃ rakṣito yuddhe mahāntaṃ prāptavāñ jayam
english: Thus in manifold forms do I range over this earth, and over the realm of Brahmā, O son of Kuntī, and the eternal realm of cows; guarded by me in battle, you have won a mighty victory.

sanskrit: yas tu te so 'grato yāti yuddhe saṃpraty upasthite taṃ viddhi rudraṃ kaunteya devadevaṃ kapardinam
english: And he who goes before you when the battle is joined — know him to be Rudra, O son of Kuntī, the god of gods, the one with matted locks.

sanskrit: kālaḥ sa eva kathitaḥ krodhajeti mayā tava nihatāṃs tena vai pūrvaṃ hatavān asi vai ripūn
english: That same one I have named to you as Time, born of wrath; those foes already slain by him, those have you in truth struck down.

sanskrit: aprameyaprabhāvaṃ taṃ devadevam umāpatim namasva devaṃ prayato viśveśaṃ haram avyayam
english: That god of gods of immeasurable power, the lord of Umā — bow down, intent and reverent, to the god Hara, the Lord of the Universe, the imperishable.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca brahman sumahad ākhyānaṃ bhavatā parikīrtitam yac chrutvā munayaḥ sarve vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: O brāhmaṇa, a most lofty narrative has been recounted by you, on hearing which all the sages have passed into the utmost wonder.

sanskrit: idaṃ śatasahasrād dhi bhāratākhyānavistarāt āmathya matimanthena jñānodadhim anuttamam
english: For out of the hundred thousand verses of the vast Bhārata narrative, by the churning-staff of the intellect this incomparable ocean of knowledge has been churned —

sanskrit: navanītaṃ yathā dadhno malayāc candanaṃ yathā āraṇyakaṃ ca vedebhya oṣadhibhyo 'mṛtaṃ yathā
english: — as butter is drawn from curds, as sandal from the Malaya hills, as the Āraṇyaka from the Vedas, as the nectar of immortality from the healing herbs —

sanskrit: samuddhṛtam idaṃ brahman kathāmṛtam anuttamam taponidhe tvayoktaṃ hi nārāyaṇakathāśrayam
english: — so has this peerless nectar of story been drawn up, O brāhmaṇa; for it has been spoken by you, O treasury of austerity, resting upon the tale of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: sa hīśo bhagavān devaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhāvanaḥ aho nārāyaṇaṃ tejo durdarśaṃ dvijasattama
english: For he is the Lord, the blessed god, the inmost soul and source of all beings; ah, hard to behold is the splendour of Nārāyaṇa, O best of the twice-born!

sanskrit: yatrāviśanti kalpānte sarve brahmādayaḥ surāḥ ṛṣayaś ca sagandharvā yac ca kiṃ cic carācaram na tato 'sti paraṃ manye pāvanaṃ divi ceha ca
english: Into whom, at the end of an aeon, all the gods led by Brahmā enter, and the sages with the gandharvas, and whatever moving or unmoving thing there is — than him I deem there is nothing higher or more purifying, in heaven or here on earth.

sanskrit: sarvāśramābhigamanaṃ sarvatīrthāvagāhanam na tathā phaladaṃ cāpi nārāyaṇakathā yathā
english: The visiting of all hermitages, the bathing at all sacred fords — none of these is so fruitful as the tale of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: sarvathā pāvitāḥ smeha śrutvemām āditaḥ kathām harer viśveśvarasyeha sarvapāpapraṇāśanīm
english: In every way are we here made pure, having heard from the beginning this story of Hari, the Lord of the Universe — a tale that destroys all sins.

sanskrit: na citraṃ kṛtavāṃs tatra yad āryo me dhanaṃjayaḥ vāsudevasahāyo yaḥ prāptavāñ jayam uttamam
english: It is no marvel that my noble forebear Dhanaṃjaya wrought such deeds there — he who, with Vāsudeva for his ally, attained the highest victory.

sanskrit: na cāsya kiṃ cid aprāpyaṃ manye lokeṣv api triṣu trailokyanātho viṣṇuḥ sa yasyāsīt sāhyakṛt sakhā
english: And I deem there was nothing unattainable for him in all the three worlds, he for whom Viṣṇu, the Lord of the three worlds, was the friend who lent his aid.

sanskrit: dhanyāś ca sarva evāsan brahmaṃs te mama pūrvakāḥ hitāya śreyase caiva yeṣām āsīj janārdanaḥ
english: And blessed, O brāhmaṇa, were all those forebears of mine, for whose good and welfare Janārdana stood.

sanskrit: tapasāpi na dṛśyo hi bhagavāṃl lokapūjitaḥ yaṃ dṛṣṭavantas te sākṣāc chrīvatsāṅkavibhūṣaṇam
english: For the blessed one, worshipped of the worlds, is not to be seen even by austerity — yet they beheld him face to face, adorned with the Śrīvatsa mark.

sanskrit: tebhyo dhanyataraś caiva nāradaḥ parameṣṭhijaḥ na cālpatejasam ṛṣiṃ vedmi nāradam avyayam śvetadvīpaṃ samāsādya yena dṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃ hariḥ
english: And more blessed than they is Nārada, the son of the Supreme One; nor do I count the imperishable sage Nārada as one of slender splendour, for, reaching the White Island, by him was Hari himself beheld.

sanskrit: devaprasādānugataṃ vyaktaṃ tat tasya darśanam yad dṛṣṭavāṃs tadā devam aniruddhatanau sthitam
english: Plainly that vision of his came in the train of the god's grace, in that he then beheld the god abiding in the form of Aniruddha.

sanskrit: badarīm āśramaṃ yat tu nāradaḥ prādravat punaḥ naranārāyaṇau draṣṭuṃ kiṃ nu tatkāraṇaṃ mune
english: But that Nārada hastened again to the hermitage of Badarī to behold Nara and Nārāyaṇa — what, O sage, was the cause of that?

sanskrit: śvetadvīpān nivṛttaś ca nāradaḥ parameṣṭhijaḥ badarīm āśramaṃ prāpya samāgamya ca tāv ṛṣī
english: And Nārada, the son of the Supreme One, returning from the White Island, having reached the hermitage of Badarī and met with those two sages —

sanskrit: kiyantaṃ kālam avasat kāḥ kathāḥ pṛṣṭavāṃś ca saḥ śvetadvīpād upāvṛtte tasmin vā sumahātmani
english: — for how long did he dwell there, and what discourses did he ask of them, when that most great-souled one had returned from the White Island?

sanskrit: kim abrūtāṃ mahātmānau naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī tad etan me yathātattvaṃ sarvam ākhyātum arhasi
english: What did those two great-souled sages, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, say? All this you ought to tell me in full accordance with the truth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca namo bhagavate tasmai vyāsāyāmitatejase yasya prasādād vakṣyāmi nārāyaṇakathām imām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Homage to that blessed Vyāsa of measureless splendour, by whose grace I shall recount this tale of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: prāpya śvetaṃ mahādvīpaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca harim avyayam nivṛtto nārado rājaṃs tarasā merum āgamat hṛdayenodvahan bhāraṃ yad uktaṃ paramātmanā
english: Having reached the great White Island and beheld the imperishable Hari, Nārada, on his return, O king, came swiftly to Meru, bearing in his heart the burden of what had been spoken by the Supreme Soul.

sanskrit: paścād asyābhavad rājann ātmanaḥ sādhvasaṃ mahat yad gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ kṣemī punar ihāgataḥ
english: Afterward, O king, a great trembling came over his spirit, in that, having gone so far a road, he had come back here again safe and sound.

sanskrit: tato meroḥ pracakrāma parvataṃ gandhamādanam nipapāta ca khāt tūrṇaṃ viśālāṃ badarīm anu
english: Then he set forth from Meru toward Mount Gandhamādana, and descended swiftly from the sky beside the wide-spreading Badarī.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa dadṛśe devau purāṇāv ṛṣisattamau tapaś carantau sumahad ātmaniṣṭhau mahāvratau
english: There he beheld the two ancient gods, foremost of sages, performing mighty austerity, fixed upon the Self, steadfast in great vows —

sanskrit: tejasābhyadhikau sūryāt sarvalokavirocanāt śrīvatsalakṣaṇau pūjyau jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇau
english: — surpassing in splendour the Sūrya that illumines all the worlds, bearing the Śrīvatsa mark, worthy of worship, wearing crowns of matted hair —

sanskrit: jālapādabhujau tau tu pādayoś cakralakṣaṇau vyūḍhoraskau dīrghabhujau tathā muṣkacatuṣkiṇau
english: — their hands and feet webbed, marked with the sign of the wheel upon their soles, broad-chested, long-armed, and bearing the fourfold sign —

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭidantāv aṣṭadaṃṣṭrau meghaughasadṛśasvanau svāsyau pṛthulalāṭau ca suhanū subhrunāsikau
english: — with sixty teeth and eight tusks, their voices like a mass of thunderclouds, fair of face and broad of brow, well-jawed, with handsome brows and noses —

sanskrit: ātapatreṇa sadṛśe śirasī devayos tayoḥ evaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃpannau mahāpuruṣasaṃjñitau
english: — the heads of those two gods like parasols: endowed with such marks, they were known by the name of the Great Persons.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā nārado hṛṣṭas tābhyāṃ ca pratipūjitaḥ svāgatenābhibhāṣyātha pṛṣṭaś cānāmayaṃ tadā
english: Beholding the two, Nārada rejoiced, and was honoured by them in return; greeted with words of welcome, he was then asked after his well-being.

sanskrit: babhūvāntargatamatir nirīkṣya puruṣottamau sadogatās tatra ye vai sarvabhūtanamaskṛtāḥ
english: Gazing upon those supreme persons, his mind turned inward — recalling those who, present in the assembly there, are saluted by all beings:

sanskrit: śvetadvīpe mayā dṛṣṭās tādṛśāv ṛṣisattamau iti saṃcintya manasā kṛtvā cābhipradakṣiṇam upopaviviśe tatra pīṭhe kuśamaye śubhe
english: 'On the White Island I beheld two such foremost sages' — thus reflecting in his mind, and making his reverent circuit about them, he seated himself there upon a fair seat made of kuśa-grass.

sanskrit: tatas tau tapasāṃ vāsau yaśasāṃ tejasām api ṛṣī śamadamopetau kṛtvā pūrvāhṇikaṃ vidhim
english: Then those two sages, the abode of austerities, of glories, and of splendours, possessed of calm and self-restraint, having performed the rite of the forenoon —

sanskrit: paścān nāradam avyagrau pādyārghyābhyāṃ prapūjya ca pīṭhayoś copaviṣṭau tau kṛtātithyāhnikau nṛpa
english: — thereafter, unhurried, having honoured Nārada with water for his feet and the guest-offering, those two seated themselves upon their seats, their rites of hospitality and of the day fulfilled, O king.

sanskrit: teṣu tatropaviṣṭeṣu sa deśo 'bhivyarājata ājyāhutimahājvālair yajñavāṭo 'gnibhir yathā
english: When they were seated there, that place shone resplendent, as a sacrificial enclosure shines with the great flames of its fires fed by oblations of clarified butter.

sanskrit: atha nārāyaṇas tatra nāradaṃ vākyam abravīt sukhopaviṣṭaṃ viśrāntaṃ kṛtātithyaṃ sukhasthitam
english: Then Nārāyaṇa there spoke these words to Nārada, who was seated at ease, rested, his hospitality received, and abiding in comfort:

sanskrit: apīdānīṃ sa bhagavān paramātmā sanātanaḥ śvetadvīpe tvayā dṛṣṭa āvayoḥ prakṛtiḥ parā
english: 'Has that blessed one, the eternal Supreme Soul, the higher nature of us both, now indeed been beheld by you on the White Island?'
